newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - August diesel tips higher.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - August diesel tips higher.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps for August tipped higher at midday on Wednesday with traders hopeful that prices would recover after its recent selloff, traders said.
August gas oil swaps were last quoted 15 cents per barrel higher from Tuesday's quotes at $23.70/$23.90.
July gas oil swaps however, were hovering around its previous day's quotes at $23.25/$23.45.
The higher outright quotes for August have also narrowed the jet/gasoil spread or regrade to plus $0.45/$0.65, compared to $0.80/$1.00 on Tuesday.
The July jet/gas oil regrade was unchanged at $0.20/0.40.
Brokers said the gas oil intermonth spread has also narrowed as a result.
Traders said the higher August quotes were indicative that the market is confident that the current bearish sentiment would improve in the forward month.
"After yesterday's sell off, prices may recover as the cash market may have been rid of all of its surplus supplies by then," one trader said.
Prompt physical gas oil was traded at $22.90 per barrel, the lowest in nearly a year. A Japanese trading house have purchased a 150,000 barrels lifting June 25-29 cargo from a major.
Traders said prices are likely to stabilise and consolidate around this level. Most were optimistic that prices would recover in the near term.
Activities in the swaps market is also expected to be quiet after the flurry of trades seen early this week.
Fuel oil swaps were quoted lower. Both July and August were indicated at $98.00/$99.00, about $1.25 off from Tuesday's quotes.
Brokers said levels have fallen because the weakness in crude futures. Brent futures in July settled six-cents off at $17.50 a barrel.
